title: Invariants of a Tseitin step
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the first, second, third, fourth, and auxiliary literals be literals on $n$ coordinates. Let the remaining original literals and remaining auxiliary literals be lists. Suppose the indices in the list beginning with the four original literals are pairwise distinct, the indices in the auxiliary list beginning with the auxiliary literal are pairwise distinct, and the two index sets are disjoint. Then the list obtained by negating the auxiliary literal and following it by the third and fourth original literals and the remaining original literals has pairwise distinct indices; the remaining auxiliary list has pairwise distinct indices; and these two index sets are disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: Five specified literals are on $n$ coordinates
The original list beginning with the four specified literals has pairwise distinct indices
The auxiliary list beginning with the specified auxiliary literal has pairwise distinct indices
The original and auxiliary index sets are disjoint
